text:
Maya Chen: Thinking about the console UX for sampling + routing: should per-route saved filters override model-level sampling hints or just surface a combined cost preview?
Samir Patel: +1 question — we have two concerns: correctness (which filters actually apply) and predictability (what cost SLO the user sees).
Liam O'Neill: My vote: show both. route filter precedence still wins for results, but show an explicit "effective sampling" card that explains model vs route sampling and estimated tokens.
Maya Chen: Love the "effective sampling" card idea. UX note: users keep getting surprised when a per-model low-sample rate hides traffic that the route owner expects to see.
Carol Jenkins: We also need a fallback hint when a route-level quota blocks requests and we route to a cheaper model. Something like: "Routed to quantized-x because route quota exceeded — results may differ" with a link to diff tool.
Samir Patel: Agreed. Ideally the console should show that as a trace/span in the route inspector so SREs can correlate spikes with fallback events.
Liam O'Neill: low-effort prototype for the card:
```
Effective sampling:
- route_filter: traffic=prod only
- model_hint: sample_rate=0.1
- effective: sample_rate=0.05 (after prefix caching + route apply)
Estimated cost delta: -37% tokens
```
Maya Chen: Nice. Also add a quick toggle: "Preview results with model sampling applied" so users can simulate.
Carol Jenkins: For the toggle, warn about accuracy drift. Maybe have a small inline metric: "preview matches live: 78%" based on historical overlap.
Samir Patel: For telemetry, we should record three fields per query: route_sampling_applied, model_sampling_hint, effective_sampling_rate. That will let us audit mismatches.
Maya Chen: Can deploy-bot emit a check when the new inspector flag is on so we can test on canary routes? @deploy-bot you up for a small hook? :slightly_smiling_face:
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled job created: ci/console-inspector/canary-sampling-check (runs hourly) :white_check_mark:
Liam O'Neill: Ops question: do we store the "effective_sampling" in the saved query snapshot? If the user updates filters later it could change what the saved query returns.
Maya Chen: I think a saved query should capture the saved filters, and the snapshot capture should include the effective_sampling at time of snapshot as a readonly metadata field. That way we can surface regressions.
Carol Jenkins: UX copy: when saving, show "Snapshot includes effective sampling metadata — results may change if model or route policies update" with a link to changelog diff.
Samir Patel: Implementation note: telemetry event size will grow. We should compress sampling fields into a single enum when possible: e.g., sampling_mode:[route-dominant, model-hint, combined].
Liam O'Neill: Also add a quick CLI to reproduce: `ri console-sim --route R123 --query 'SELECT ...' --preview-sampling` - prints simulated effective tokens + fallback hints.
Maya Chen: Action items: Samir to add telemetry fields, Liam to prototype the effective-sampling card and CLI, Carol to draft copy for snapshot warning, I'll wire the toggle in the console. Can we try a canary next week?
Samir Patel: Yep, I'll open an RFC and add the telemetry schema.
Liam O'Neill: I'll push a mock in Figma and a minimal backend to surface the card on canary routes.
Carol Jenkins: I'll draft the copy and add examples of fallback notices.
Maya Chen: Thanks all. If anyone wants to test the hourly job it posts results to #eng-sre by default.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: first canary run completed — 12 routes checked, 2 fallback events detected, summary posted to #eng-sre: link
